summary:
When scientists and space agencies plan missions to the Moon or Mars, they need to test rovers, drills, and hardware on Earth first. But finding the exact geological lookalikes—like matching a specific Martian crater's slope and roughness to an Earth desert—has always been messy and scattered across different tools.

That’s why I built TERRA. It’s a planetary analog discovery platform that lets researchers easily compare Earth terrains against official lunar and Martian data. Instead of relying on black-box AI guesses, TERRA uses real open-source datasets (like Copernicus GLO-30 for Earth, LRO LOLA for the Moon, and MGS MOLA for Mars) and runs math-based geomorphological calculations for slope, roughness, relief, and thermal inertia. With an interactive Free Roam coordinate inspector, side-by-side A-to-Z comparisons, and explicit mission-testing protocols, TERRA makes picking and validating field sites fast, accurate, and completely transparent.
details:
TERRA is a web platform for cross-planetary terrain comparison. You can click anywhere on Earth, Moon, or Mars using the Free Roam map, instantly inspect coordinates and place names, and run a side-by-side comparison against any other world. The app breaks down exact metrics like elevation, slope gradients, local relief, albedo, and thermal inertia using deterministic formulas derived from real space agency data.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Planning rover deployments or astronaut training requires rigorous field testing. TERRA saves researchers hours of manual GIS work by instantly surfacing the best Earth analogs, auto-highlighting matching zones, and providing concrete Mission Testing Protocols—such as identifying basaltic regolith for rover wheel traction tests or hyper-saline basins for thermal drill trials.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Frontend: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and MapLibre GL JS styled with a clean, high-end aerospace dark theme.
  • Data & Science Pipeline: Python, Rasterio, and NumPy for processing global Digital Elevation Models.
  • Development Workflow: Built entirely in Visual Studio Code using GitHub Copilot for rapid, architecture-driven code generation. Everything is designed to be fast, highly responsive, and effortlessly intuitive.
